items.sentence: The MHRA says large studies of millions of children have found no evidence that vaccines cause autism, and reaffirms the safety of childhood vaccination.
items.note: Stated in the retrieved search summary of the source page.

items.sentence: The MHRA's Chief Safety Officer, Dr Alison Cave, says large, well-conducted studies of millions of children worldwide consistently show no evidence that vaccines cause autism.
items.note: Stated in the retrieved search summary of the source page.

items.sentence: The statement cites a study of 2.56 million US children that found no link between MMR vaccination before age 2 and autism.
items.note: Stated in the retrieved search summary of the source page.

items.sentence: The MHRA has published a statement reaffirming the safety of childhood vaccination.
items.note: Stated in the retrieved search summary of the source page.

items.sentence: Dr Alison Cave, the MHRA's Chief Safety Officer, says that multiple large, well-conducted studies involving millions of children worldwide consistently show no evidence that vaccines cause autism.

items.sentence: The notes to the statement cite a study of 2.56 million children in the United States that found no association between MMR vaccination before age 2 and childhood autism.
